rules.text: Low coolant, visible coolant loss, and overheating indicate a coolant leak.
Overheating with a temperature warning and steam is consistent with a stuck thermostat.
Clicking, dim lights, and hard starting indicate insufficient battery power.
A charging warning with dim lights and failing accessories points to alternator output.
A no-crank condition despite a charging warning can indicate a failed starter motor.
Brake squeal or grinding with a warning light indicates severely worn pads.
Brake vibration and pulling with squeal are consistent with uneven rotor surfaces.
A spongy pedal with a brake warning suggests air or fluid loss in the hydraulic lines.
Misfire, rough idle, and hard starting are characteristic of ignition faults.
Hesitation with poor economy and misfire suggests restricted fuel delivery.
Sulfur exhaust odor, a warning light, and power loss suggest an emissions-system fault.
Low oil pressure with a visible leak and burning-oil odor requires immediate attention.
Slipping, delayed engagement, and a transmission burning smell indicate fluid or clutch trouble.
Steering vibration, pulling, and uneven tire wear point to alignment or suspension wear.
Overheating combined with low coolant supports coolant loss.
A clicking no-crank and dim headlights are strong signs of a weak battery.
Grinding together with brake squeal commonly indicates pad wear.
A misfire and check-engine light commonly accompany ignition faults.
